newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish markka seen in ERM by end-Oct at 3.05 - poll.
newsitem.headline: Finnish markka seen in ERM by end-Oct at 3.05 - poll.

text.p: The Finnish markka is expected to join Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) by end-October this year at a central parity exchange rate of 3.05 to the German mark, according to the majority view in a Reuters poll.
Twelve of 22 dealers, analysts and economists at banks and corporate treasury departments saw the markka joining ERM in October with the mean of their central parity forecasts at 3.05.
Six expected a link to take place already in September with a mean of 3.05. Three participants voted for November with a mean central parity exchange rate of 3.06 markka per mark.
One large bank saw the markka entering ERM in December. It forecast the central parity of the markka at 3.08 to the German mark.

Six out of the 22 saw the markka's central parity at 3.05. Moreover, fourteen banks and corporates forecast the central parity to be something between 3.05 and 3.06. The range of all forecasts was 3.03-3.08.
In the previous market poll conducted in June, the mean of 19 forecasts of the markka's central parity exchange rate against the mark was 3.10 in a range of 3.05-3.12.
The new poll was carried out on Monday and Tuesday this week. The forecasts were collected on an anonymous basis. Noone of the 22 participants expected the markka to remain floating.

Forecasts by: Aktia Bank, Bank of America (London), Banque Indosuez (Stockholm), CD Derivatives Ltd, Davy Protos, Den Danske Bank (Copenhagen), Enskilda Banken Helsinki, Enso, Handelsbanken Markets Finland, Huhtamaki Finance, Interbank, IVO, Kemira, Kesko, Merita Bank, Neste, Nokia, OKOBANK, Postipankki, SOK, Unibank (Copenhagen) and UPM-Kymmene.
